world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.quote: Stress is lexically determined in Arguni and can fall on any syllable (see the examples in 15). Penultimate stress is the most common. (16) shows two stress minimal pairs. (15) Final stress: mardené ‘in three days’ / Penultimate stress: uririá”ir ‘ancestors’ / Antipenultimate stress: putíggyafwa ‘beach’ / Preantipenultimate stress: aérafai ‘cannot’ (16) ússu ‘penis’ / ussú (trucated form of ussúfir ‘you go down’ or of ussú’e ‘you (don’t) like’) / gána ‘I am’/‘I am from’ / ganá ‘I put’. Some verb lexemes specify that stress must fall on the first-attaching prefix, e.g. -ssa ‘go up’.
new_statements.citation: Milano, Pietro. 2025. A sketch grammar of Arguni. Research MA thesis, Utrecht University. §3.2 Stress
new_statements.rule_in_words: In Arguni (sister variety of Erokwanas in the Arguni–Mbaruan–Yarikman dialect continuum) word stress is lexically specified: it may sit on the final, penultimate, antepenultimate or pre-antepenultimate syllable, with penultimate the most frequent, and there are stress minimal pairs (ússu/ussú, gána/ganá). Certain verb roots (e.g. -ssa 'go up', -agin 'give') require stress on the first-attaching prefix (subject prefix, pluractional fa-, or CV reduplicant). No source states the Erokwanas pattern itself.
new_statements.exceptions: Verbs like -ssa 'go up' and -agin 'give' put stress on the first prefix rather than the root (p. 16 and fn. 18); partial reduplication copies the stressed syllable and keeps penultimate stress (§4); plural possessor suffix -si shifts stress (p. 30ff.); IPA transcriptions in the quote are omitted because the PDF's TIPA font extracts garbled (e.g. [mar.de."ne:] for [mar.de.ˈneː]); read them in the PDF.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level; citation forms and inflected verbs from 2024-25 fieldwork in Arguni village (Berau Gulf island). Orthographic acute marks stress. Describes Arguni (argu1237), NOT Erokwanas/Yarikman (erok1237); Milano says the three varieties form one dialect/language group whose distinctness is still to be assessed (pp. 8-10).
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted statement describes ARGUNI (argu1237, ISO agf), not Erokwanas/Yarikman (erok1237). Glottolog: "Arguni-Bedoanas-Erokwanas forms a dialect continuum" (Smits & Voorhoeve 1992); Milano 2025 calls it the Arguni-Mbaruan-Yarikman dialect/language group (Glottolog family name 'Nuta') and reports 79% Arguni-Mbaruan and 87% Mbaruan-Yarikman lexical similarity from Jacobson Holmström (2024). No accessible source states where stress falls in Erokwanas itself. File the statement under argu1237; for erok1237 it is a sister-variety proxy only.

sources.citation: Milano, Pietro. 2025. A sketch grammar of Arguni. Research MA thesis, Utrecht University. §3.2 Stress
sources.quote: Stress is lexically determined in Arguni and can fall on any syllable (see the examples in 15). Penultimate stress is the most common. (16) shows two stress minimal pairs. (15) Final stress: mardené ‘in three days’ / Penultimate stress: uririá”ir ‘ancestors’ / Antipenultimate stress: putíggyafwa ‘beach’ / Preantipenultimate stress: aérafai ‘cannot’ (16) ússu ‘penis’ / ussú (trucated form of ussúfir ‘you go down’ or of ussú’e ‘you (don’t) like’) / gána ‘I am’/‘I am from’ / ganá ‘I put’. Some verb lexemes specify that stress must fall on the first-attaching prefix, e.g. -ssa ‘go up’.
sources.note: §3.2 Stress, p. 16: stress in ARGUNI (argu1237, sister variety of Erokwanas in the same dialect continuum) is lexically determined, can fall on any syllable (final, penult, antepenult, pre-antepenult examples), penultimate most common, two stress minimal pairs, some verbs require stress on the first prefix. Nothing said about stress in Yarikman/Erokwanas specifically; Erokwanas mentioned only for classification, village names (Goras, Darembang), and the 87% lexical similarity with Mbaruan reported from Jacobson Holmström (2024).
